name: plan-medium-council
description: The Medium Council (0.8.3): the middle of three planning chains (plan-mini-council, plan-medium-council, plan-high-council). It runs the planning stages with three proposers (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, MiMo V2.6 Pro, Gemini 3.8 Flash), an alternatives stage (GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and GLM-5.3 Flash; every proposer also debates the architectures), one deep-dive seat (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) and a layered review panel of seven named judges in three layers: layer 1 GLM-5.3 Flash, MiMo V2.6 Pro, GPT-6 Luna; layer 2 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Claude Haiku 5.5; layer 3 GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5. Exactly these seven vote, seven judges from five companies (GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6.1 Sol are one company, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Claude Opus 5.5 are one company); DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, MiMo V2.6 Pro, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and GLM-5.3 Flash each both propose and judge, which is why "judging" is "all-roles". Every layer has at least two judges. A layer is asked only when every layer below it signed off, and a layer signs off when all its judges do. Any objection at a lower layer sends the draft to the reviser and the climb starts again at layer 1; a round ends only when layer 3 gives its verdict, a sign-off or an objection. This chain allows 3 such overseer rounds (maxOverseerRounds) and, inside one round, 2 revisions of layer 1 and 1 of layer 2 (layerRevisions). When either limit is reached the run stops, resumable and NOT agreed, and you choose: continue (it extends the limit that was reached; the run's spending limit still applies), or finish (the dispute stage and the handoff run and the result stays "not agreed"), or revise the draft yourself. Claude Haiku 5.5 (layer 2) and Claude Opus 5.5 (layer 3) are answered through your own Claude subscription (provider external, subscription:haiku-5.5, subscription:opus-5.5): like the criteria, skeleton, build, revise and handoff stages, each pauses the run (exit 3) until it is answered, and the answers should come from a separate fresh session, not the one that wrote the plan. Without a Claude subscription, replace each of those seats with its API seat: {"provider":"openrouter","model":"anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5","maxTokens":128000,"lab":"haiku5.5","extra":{"reasoning":{"effort":"high"}},"layer":2}; {"provider":"openrouter","model":"anthropic/claude-opus-5.5","maxTokens":128000,"lab":"opus5.5","extra":{"reasoning":{"effort":"high"}},"layer":3}; the other stages still need a Claude Code session. answer_back is on: a judge's own earlier objection is shown back to it, and only that judge can close it. The criteria, skeleton, build, revise and handoff stages need a Claude Code session (provider external): they pause the run (exit 3) until the session answers. Every API seat reasons at high, or at the model's own default where that is higher (the harness sends these no effort setting: GLM-5.3 Flash at max); no Grok, no Kimi. Output caps are the largest reply the harness knows for each model: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 393,216; MiMo V2.6 Pro and GLM-5.3 Flash 131,072; GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna 128,000; Gemini 3.8 Flash 65,536. Dry run (0.8.3, prices of 2026-10-18, the dry run's assumed sizes): $7.16 expected (every overseer round ends after one climb through the layers) and an upper estimate of $23.04 (every allowed revision used in every overseer round), about $7.16 plus a Claude subscription. The upper estimate leaves out the in-pass re-asks (up to 2 per seat), up to 2 consecutive passes that re-ask a silent seat, the explicit asks of a silent judge, answer-back calls, the memory block judge calls read from overseer round 2 on (up to 10000 tokens per call, paid input that neither figure prices) and the larger prompt the top layer reads, so it is not a ceiling: the limit you type is what stops spending. No proposer's cap is below the most the harness will retry its model at, so a proposal cut off at its cap is not asked again with a bigger one. The upper estimate ($23.04) is above the default cap of $7. On the command line that cap is only a suggestion. The Claude Desktop bundle's default Spend ceiling of $10 is a hard ceiling nobody can type above, so with that default a run that uses its whole allowance stops at the ceiling (the expected figure and the cheapest end, $6.75, fit under it). Type a limit above the upper estimate to keep the run from stopping at its limit unless a call outside the plan adds up; a lower limit, even the expected figure, can stop it there (exit 4, resumable with a higher total). This roster has not run, and none of its mechanisms has been measured. Price your task with `npm run dry` and get an explicit go before any paid run.
summary: Seven judges in three layers; three overseer rounds. Haiku and Opus via your Claude plan.
